**Finding: compliant** — no redline proposed.

The document contains no non-compete or field-of-use restraint on Sparkling, so the rule's preferred position is met:

- **§3 "Restrictions on Use" (p0031–p0039)** is purely licence-scope: no copying beyond backup/AS400, no copying Documentation beyond internal use, no assignment/sublicence/export of the Work, no reverse engineering, no use outside the Agreement, and no use of the Work as a service bureau. Each restriction attaches to *the Work* (Garman's software), not to our business, products or procurement — nothing bars us from acquiring, building or licensing competing routing systems.
- **§19 (p0133)** is a mutual employee non-solicitation (term plus one year), not a restraint of trade; it falls under the non-solicitation rule, so I did not flag the same term twice here.
- **§20 / general matters (p0135–p0149)** contain no exclusivity, minimum-purchase, territory or competing-products covenant; the only "exclusive" references are a non-exclusive licence grant, a remedies clause and non-exclusive jurisdiction — all neutral or favourable to us.
- **§14 confidentiality (p0098)** expressly carves out independently developed information, which preserves our internal development freedom.

No walk-away or fallback analysis is needed since there is no restriction to narrow.
